### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (literal, 59 pages)`
- **22** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `05c79bd3942ae20608f4440ca01177fa8889cf41` — the merge of head `c527c7ac1c1a9ea7ec41feb6d88ee2d4c07311ea` into base `57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 05c79bd3942ae20608f4440ca01177fa8889cf41 && git checkout 05c79bd3942ae20608f4440ca01177fa8889cf41
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b c527c7ac1c1a9ea7ec41feb6d88ee2d4c07311ea && git checkout -B drift-repro 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b && git merge --no-ff c527c7ac1c1a9ea7ec41feb6d88ee2d4c07311ea

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `99dc6d0002db3027e6749a53cb7ec5174c87fcfc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/metadata-list-registry.ts + packages/spec/src/system/metadata-list-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-types-translation-parity-36886.test.ts, packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.metadata-list-columns.test.ts, the 11 packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/*.metadata-forms.generated.ts bundles and the de and fr source-hashes files (generated; read only for agreement with the registry and the extractor), content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/services/builtinComponents.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/anchors.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceListPage.servedListColumns-36860.test.tsx, .changeset/36860-metadata-list-columns-batch.md
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

A fresh record for part (b) of card #36860, not a delta. Inputs: the card body and all eight comments (the six read for #36881, plus the seat correction 7126249846 and the dev report 7127365265), the PR body, the 26-file net diff `origin/main...pr-36926` (merge-base `151e8123c226`, the merge of part (a)), and the head's check-runs.

No must-fix.

**S1 (should-fix) — the dispatcher's translated types listing omits `Vary: Accept-Language`.** Both new call sites in `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` (near lines 1389 and 2893) answer `deps.success(translated)`. The same file states the rule: a `/meta` read owes `Vary: Accept-Language` on a body translated per request, and `successWithHeaders` is "the ONE place this domain builds such an answer"; `answerMetaList` and the item answer both use it. `RestServer`'s listing sets the header in `meta-collection-routes.ts` before it sends. After this PR the dispatcher's `GET /meta` and `GET /meta/types` bodies vary by `Accept-Language` with no `Vary`, so a cache between the host and the reader may serve one reader's language to another, and the PR's claim that both doors answer alike holds for the body only. Fix: answer through `successWithHeaders(deps, translated, { Vary: 'Accept-Language' })` at both sites, and have the parity test read the header beside the body.

**S2 (should-fix) — the card's zh screenshots are not delivered, and this PR says `Fixes #36860`.** The card's acceptance ends "screenshots (zh) of Hooks, Flows and Jobs lists in the PR body". The body carries no image. Part (a) was reviewed on the understanding that they land with the closing PR. Closable without a head move: add the three screenshots to the body, or the maintainer waives the bullet on the card.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`METADATA_LIST_REGISTRY` grows from 1 to 27 entries: right.** The schema shapes and `defineList` that part (a) merged are untouched; this diff only adds entries. Every one of the card's 18 first-batch types is present, with the keys corrected as the supplementary analysis (7122828117) and the dev's report on (a) said: `action.objectName`, `api.objectParams.object` and `.operation`, `assignment_rule.entries` and `active`, `mapping.targetObject` / `mode` / `sourceFormat`, `picklist.options`, `doc.group` and `tags`, `agent.model.model`, no `email_template.category`, `seed` without name or label. `flow` declares `type` only, as the seat route ruled. `object` takes the set that actually rendered on `main` (the `anchors.ts` one). Spot-read against the schemas at head: `seed.object` and `mode`, `agent.role` and `active`, `skill.tools` and `active`, `tool.objectName`, `doc.group` and `tags`, `dataset.object` are declared keys. The full check is the reconciliation test, whose roster now names all 27; its CI lane is still running (see the check-runs note).
- **Served surface: `/meta/types` carries `list` on 26 more entries: right.** No code change serves it; part (a)'s `getMetaTypes()` reads the registry. Additive for every client.
- **`translateMetaTypesListing` (new export of `@objectstack/rest`): right.** It is the body `translateMetaTypesResponse` had on `main`, moved. `RestServer` now delegates to it with the same i18n service, the same locale reader and the same options (`buildTranslationBundle`, `extractLocale` and `translateOptionsFor` were already one-line delegates to the gate module's `translationBundleOf`, `metaRequestLocale` and `metaTranslateOptions`). `RestServer`'s answer is unchanged.
- **The runtime dispatcher translates `GET /meta` and `GET /meta/types`: right in the body, incomplete in the headers (S1).** The served labels, form labels, list headers and schema titles change from always-English to the request's locale. An en request and a host with no i18n service answer as before; both are pinned as controls.
- **52 new `metadataForms.TYPE.fields.PATH.label` leaves in 11 bundles: right, with one unstated side effect (N2).** The zh-CN bundle read in full for the diff agrees with the registry: one leaf per column path the type's form does not label, dotted paths kept as one quoted key. The slot is the existing one; no translation schema changes.
- **Console: the eight `listColumns` declarations and the second `object` one are removed: right.** What stays is what the schema cannot say: `field` appends the server-stamped `object` through `listExtraColumns`; `position` appends `_holderCount` and `_grantedPermissionSets` the same way; `view.type`, `book.audience` and `sharing_rule.sharedWith` keep their renderers through `listCells`; `sharing_rule` appends `_packageId`. The page list's `route` column, which named no `PageSchema` key, is gone. Visible changes a reader will notice are in N3.
- **`i18n-standard.mdx`: right.** It adds the list-column row and says the three resolvers run in `GET /api/v1/meta`. True on both doors after this PR.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, each `patch`. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right against the tree. No schema file changes, no authorable-surface or api-surface shard moves, and no key, value or type an author can write is added, removed or re-meant. The registry is a platform constant and the 52 leaves use the slot that already exists. `none` takes `patch` by AGENTS.md step 3, and the one new export (`translateMetaTypesListing`) is a non-protocol widening, which also ships `patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: 26 more entries carry `list`, one new export, and the dispatcher's listing gains translation. Nothing accepted before is refused. The line is in the PR body and the changeset body. With `none`, no `Skills-docs:` line is owed.
- **`@objectstack/lint` has no entry and needs none.** The only lint file in the diff is `src/i18n-walk.metadata-list-columns.test.ts`; the package's `files` are `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, so nothing in the published package changes.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` has no entry.** It is `private: true` and publishes nothing; part (a) listed it and this part drops it. Either reads as acceptable to the changeset gate.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: empty. `out_of_scope_findings`: empty.**
- **How (b) sits on (a).** It extends the registry and replaces nothing in the spec. `servedListColumns.tsx`, `registry.ts` and `useMetadata.ts` are not in the diff; the console change is only the removal of declarations that the served list now supersedes, which is the precedence (a) put in place doing its job. The `rest-server.ts` listing path is refactored to a shared function with the same behaviour. Nothing (a) merged is contradicted.
- **#36881 carry-overs, by id.**
  - N1 (served headers marked localized while the dispatcher served them untranslated): closed for the dispatcher path by the `translateMetaTypesListing` fold. A residual stays, see N1 below.
  - N2 (extractor branch unpinned): closed. The new lint test pins a form-less type (`job.schedule`), a dotted path the form leaves out (`agent` `model.model`), a form-labelled column keeping exactly one entry (`hook.events`), and one entry per registry column.
  - N3 (`listInclude` prose named `listExtraColumns` before `position` used it): closed. `position` now declares both grant columns under `listExtraColumns`, so the sentence is true. `registry.ts` itself needed no edit.
  - N4 (`defineList` jsdoc; skills debt starts with a registrar): open, not owed by this card.
  - N5 (`MetadataListViewSchema.data` accepts any provider arm): open, unchanged.
  - N6 (`MetadataListType` is `string`): open, parity with the form registry.
  - N7 (the reconciliation test hand-copies `humanizeFieldPath`): open, unchanged, and now load-bearing for 52 column paths.
  - Seat card, dispatcher serving `form` and `list` untranslated (#36886): closed in substance by this PR, subject to S1. The body says it "folds in" #36886 but carries no closing keyword for it (N4 below).
  - Seat card, `GetMetaTypesResponseSchema` lacking `schema` and `form` (#36887): open, announced as its own PR.
- **The card's owed items for (b).** Extractor pin: delivered. The `listInclude` / `position` fix: delivered through the `position` move. zh screenshots: not delivered (S2).
- **Card acceptance, the rest.** Hooks, Flows and Jobs declare the named columns. The nine console-declared types keep the same or better columns, `object` has one set. A type with no declaration still gets the default three (unchanged code). A declaration naming an undeclared key fails the reconciliation test. The plugin-registered bullet was dropped by the seat (7122844515) and stays dropped.
- **Tier.** By the seat correction 7126249846 the card counts as over 3,000 lines across its PRs, so this PR is held for the maintainer's own review whatever this record says. This record does not ready, queue or arm it.
- **Security: the new function is not a gate, and no gate moves.** `translateMetaTypesListing` lives in `meta-item-read-gate.ts` but only rewrites display strings on a listing the caller was already given. Both dispatcher sites sit after the unchanged anonymous deny and type-level admission, and call it on the result of the unchanged `getMetaTypes()`. The strings come from the platform's `metadataForms` bundle group, which `RestServer` already serves to the same callers. No permission, sharing, credential or token behaviour is taught by any hunk, hence `Security-touching: no`. The dispatcher resolves the i18n service through the existing `metaTranslationSources` helper its list and item reads already use; no new scoping decision is made here. S1 is a caching-correctness finding, not an access one: the listing holds no per-caller data beyond language.
- **SQL push-down: not applicable.** No query, id materialisation or in-app join is added; every new step reads a module constant or an in-memory bundle.
- **Author.** The PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; the body is signed by the dev session `session_01WGufzg7mFFG5b13DcQ93kf`.

### ④ Design judgment

`metadata-list-registry.ts` holds against the rulings it implements (7122828117 as routed by 7122844515) and against its first consumer, Studio's generic list, on all 27 types. The implementing files agree with it except for S1. Nits and accepted deviations:

- **N1 (residual of #36881 N1, accepted).** On a host with no i18n service or no bundle, the listing is still served in English and the console still shows served headers as they come. That now covers 27 lists, including `object`, `field` and `view`, whose `name` / `label` / `type` / `description` / `object` headers the console's own `engine.list.col.*` table used to translate for a zh reader. On such a host the type labels and forms are English too, so the list is consistent with its page. If that host shape matters, the console can fall back to its table when a served header equals its English source.
- **N2 (unstated side effect).** `resolveMetadataFormSchemaTitles` applies every `fields.PATH` key of the bundle as a JSON Schema `title`. The 52 new leaves therefore also title those nodes on the served `schema` of types with no form (`job`, `api`, `queue`, `doc`, `book`, `seed`, `mapping`, `picklist`, `translation`, `sharing_rule`, `assignment_rule`), so their schema-derived editors show these few keys translated and the rest in English. Harmless and arguably better, but neither the PR body nor the changeset says it.
- **N3 (visible list changes).** Served columns carry no width; the console's percentage widths for the moved types are gone unless `listCells` restates them (only `view.type` and `book.audience` do). The Fields list order changes from name / object / type / label to name / type / label / object, because the stamped `object` is appended. The sharing-rule header reads "Access Level" where it read "Access". The page list gains `type` and `description` for the dropped `route`.
- **N4 (PR body).** `Fixes #36860` closes the card; #36886 is folded in without a closing keyword, so the seat closes it by hand at landing or the body gains one.
- **N5.** At both dispatcher sites the translation runs inside the `try` that guards `getMetaTypes()`. A throw from translation falls through to the types-only fallback (no `entries`) instead of answering the untranslated listing. The function has no throwing path in normal use; note it when S1 is fixed.

Check-runs on the head, latest run per name, read at review time:
- `success` (18): Auto Label, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, filter.
- `skipped` (9): the opt-in, queue-only and matrix-parent lanes, the same nine as on #36881.
- **still running (19):** Build Core, Build UI Deps, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/10 through 10/10, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace.
- **not yet started:** the Test UI shards, Lint UI, Type Check UI and Build & E2E UI lanes that ran on #36881.

The gate verdicts this record leans on (the reconciliation test, the lint pin, the dispatcher parity test, the i18n bundle gates, the app-shell tests and type-check) are in the running or unstarted lanes. The PASS below is on the reading; a red on any of them is not covered by it.

**Mechanical.** `l1-face` is incomplete on this head: 23 checks succeeded, 9 skipped, 34 were still running, and none had failed. One item is flagged, `changeset`, for `@objectstack/lint`. Its only touched file is `src/i18n-walk.metadata-list-columns.test.ts`, and the package ships `files: ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md"]`, so it owes no entry. `check-governed-merges` reports NOT governed for this file list (2,834 lines). - **S1 (should-fix): the dispatcher's translated listing omits `Vary: Accept-Language`.** I checked both new sites in `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`: each answers `deps.success(translated)`. The same file states the rule at `:342`, which is that a per-request-translated body answers through `successWithHeaders` with `Vary: Accept-Language`, as its list and item reads do (`:754`, `:839`). `RestServer` sets the header on its listing. Neither #36881 nor this PR carries any, and this PR says `Fixes #36860`. **Fix:** take the three zh-CN shots on the fixed head and link them from the body. **Nits (record N1–N5; no action required):** the English-only residual without i18n; the new leaves also title schema nodes (unstated); list widths and column order shift; #36886 has no closing keyword (the seat closes it by hand); translation runs inside `getMetaTypes()`'s `try`.

## Rework delta for L1-a · head 06064a11 · 2026-11-24T09:53Z

Answers L1 7127583143 and contract review 7127569547 (both on `99dc6d00`). The PR stays a draft, held for the maintainer's own review.

- **S1, fixed in `9ce7a6d0`.** Both dispatcher sites in `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` now answer `successWithHeaders(deps, translated, { Vary: 'Accept-Language' })`. `meta-types-translation-parity-36886.test.ts` reads the header on both dispatcher doors and on `RestServer`'s (4 passed). Ablation: answering the translated body without the header reds the new case (1 failed, 3 passed), restored by `trap`. On a live showcase boot every console `GET /api/v1/meta` answered `Vary: Accept-Language, Origin, Accept-Encoding`. Record N5 (translation inside the `getMetaTypes()` try) is unchanged and noted.
- **S2, delivered.** Three zh-CN screenshots of the Hooks, Flows and Jobs lists, taken on a booted `examples/app-showcase` built from `9ce7a6d0` (the commits after it change only the changeset and tests). They are in the project's shared files under `objectstack-seat3-ux/36860-shots/` and described in the PR body's new Screenshots section.
- **S3, fixed in `9ce7a6d0` and `137ae10f`.** The changeset now carries `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` and a sentence naming record N3's visible changes: no fixed widths on the moved lists, the Fields order, the "Access Level" header, and the Pages list's type and description. On the conflict between the two reviews: #36881's L1 advice was to drop app-shell because it is private, but no repo rule requires leaving it out. `.changeset/config.json` sets `privatePackages.version: true`, so app-shell is versioned and keeps a CHANGELOG, `check-changeset-fixed` only governs the `fixed` group (where app-shell is not a member), and 201 of the 719 changesets on main name it. AGENTS.md step 3 requires an entry for what publishes and does not forbid one for a versioned private package.
